draft.hook: Most investors assume direct and regular mutual funds are different products. They are not, and the confusion is understandable.
draft.body:
Both plan types of the same mutual fund scheme share the exact same underlying portfolio, fund manager, and investment strategy. The real difference lies in how you purchase the units and what you pay for it.

Investors buy direct plan units directly from the Asset Management Company or through online investment platforms without intermediaries. Regular plans carry a higher expense ratio because they include distribution commissions paid to the intermediary, whereas direct plans do not include these commissions. The portfolio remains identical; only the cost structure and the purchase path change.
draft.call_to_action: Have you switched from regular to direct plans, or did you learn this distinction recently? Share your experience in the comments, or head to Varsity to read more about how mutual funds work.
draft.image_idea: A clean split-screen graphic showing identical portfolio charts on one side and a simplified fee breakdown on the other.

It clarifies the difference in purchase path and expense ratio without promising returns or giving investment advice, and closes by inviting comments and pointing to Varsity for further education.
